A man asked whether a husband who finds another man with his wife should kill him, and the couple were later seen doing Li'an in the mosque.
When Hilal bin Umaiya accused his wife of adultery, the Prophet told him to bring proof or be lashed, then mentioned the li'an as in the Book.
Husbands who accuse their wives of adultery, told to bring witnesses or be lashed, carry out the revealed mutual cursing; the couples separate and the child goes to the mother.
Husbands accusing wives of adultery swore li'an with them before the Prophet, who urged repentance and separated them; the mahr was not returned and the child was the mother's.
Ibn Umar reported that the Prophet separated a couple after li'an, saying one of them lies, and told the husband his mahr could not be taken back.
The Prophet separated a couple after li'an and her child resembled the accused man; Ibn Abbas said the woman the Prophet would have stoned without witnesses was another.
A husband and wife carried out li'an in the mosque after he asked whether a man finding another with his wife should kill him, and divorce was decreed.
Discussing a li'an case, Ibn Abbas said the Prophet's words about stoning a woman without proof concerned one whose open misbehaviour aroused suspicion.
Uwaimir asked whether a husband who kills a man found with his wife is killed; the Prophet disliked the question, revelation came, they performed li'an, and he divorced her.
